purpose: Amifampridine is used to treat Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS), a rare condition where your immune system attacks the connections between your nerves and muscles. It helps improve muscle strength and reduces weakness and fatigue. This medicine can make everyday activities like walking and lifting much easier.
how_it_works: Your nerves talk to your muscles by releasing a chemical called acetylcholine. In LEMS, not enough of this chemical is released, making your muscles weak. Amifampridine works by blocking tiny channels in nerve cells, which helps more acetylcholine get released so your muscles can work better.
common_side_effects: Tingling or numbness around the mouth, fingers, or toes (this is very common), stomach upset or nausea, headache, back pain, high blood pressure, and muscle cramps. These side effects are usually mild and often improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have a history of seizures, because this medicine can increase the risk of seizures. It should be used very carefully in people with kidney or liver problems, as the drug can build up in your body. Avoid taking it with other medicines that lower the seizure threshold. Tell your doctor about all your medications. Do not suddenly stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 15–30 mg per day, split into 3–4 smaller doses taken throughout the day. Your doctor will slowly increase the dose based on how you respond. The maximum dose is generally 80 mg per day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and try to space doses evenly throughout the day.
